h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר י״ח Pesach — Maamar Yud Ches

p: כְּדֵי לְטַהֲרֵנוּ מִקְּלִיפּוֹתֵינוּ וּמִטּוּמְאוֹתֵינוּ וְכוּלֵּי, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּטַּהֲרוּ נַפְשׁוֹת עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִזּוֹהֲמָתָם וְכוּלֵּי.
"In order to purify us from our spiritual husks and from our impurities, etc.; in order that the souls of Your people Israel be purified from their filth, etc."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבַקְּשִׁים: יְתוּקַּן מַה שֶּׁפָּגַמְתִּי וְכוּלֵּי וְאֶטָּהֵר וְאֶתְקַדֵּשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁל מַעְלָה וְכוּלֵּי.

And afterward [in the Leshem Yichud prayer for counting the Omer] we petition: "May whatever I have blemished be rectified, etc., and may I be purified and sanctified with the holiness from on high, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִצְוַת סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר הִיא כְּעֵין סְפִירַת שִׁבְעָה נְקִיִּים שֶׁל הָאִשָּׁה, וְהִיא הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
That is, the mitzvah of Sefiras HaOmer is analogous to a woman's counting of seven clean days, serving as preparation for the Giving of the Torah.
וּבַגְּמָרָא
And in the Gemara
(שַׁבָּת קמ"ו.):
(Shabbos 146a):

יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי פָּסְקָה זוֹהֲמָתָן וְכוּלֵּי, וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַב אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא וְכוּלֵּי: עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת לֹא פָּסְקָה זוֹהֲמָא וְכוּלֵּי, יַעֲקֹב הוֹלִיד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּהֶם שׁוּם דּוֹפִי.

"When Israel stood at Mount Sinai, their filth ceased, etc.; and this disputes Rav Abba bar Kahana, etc.: until three generations the filth did not cease, etc.—Yaakov begot twelve tribes in whom there was no blemish."
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים וְלֹא פְּלִיגִי:
And we have already explained that "both these and those are the words of the living God" and they do not actually disagree:
שֶׁבְּעוֹמֶק פָּסְקָה זוֹהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
for at the deepest root, the filth of the Serpent ceased in our father Yaakov, whose bed was complete,
וּכְתִיב
and it is written
(מִיכָה ז', כ'):
(Michah 7:20):
תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב,
"You will give truth to Yaakov,"
וּכְתִיב
and it is written
(מִשְׁלֵי י"ב, י"ט):
(Mishlei 12:19):
שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד,
"A truthful lip shall be established forever,"
וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ מִצִּדּוֹ לֹא מֵת
and likewise our father Yaakov from his own side did not die
(תַּעֲנִית ה':).
(Taanis 5b).
אַךְ עַל זַרְעוֹ לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה פְּסִיקַת זוֹהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ עַד מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, דִּכְתִיב
However, upon his descendants, the cessation of the Serpent's filth was not revealed until the Giving of the Torah, as it is written
(תְּהִלִּים פ"ב, ו'):
(Tehillim 82:6):
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם,
"I said, you are angelic beings,"
דְּלָא הֲווֹ מַיְיתֵי
so that they would not have died
(עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה'.).
(Avodah Zarah 5a).
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁפָּסְקָה אָז זוֹהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ, וְסָפְרוּ שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת לִהְיוֹת מְזוּקָּק שִׁבְעָתַיִם בְּכָל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת.
That is, the filth of the Serpent ceased then, and they counted seven weeks to be refined sevenfold across all seven attributes.
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּטַּהֲרוּ נַפְשׁוֹת עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִזּוֹהֲמָתָם וְכוּלֵּי
And this is what we recite: "in order that the souls of Your people Israel be purified from their filth, etc."
שֶׁאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל בְּכָל שָׁנָה מִתְעוֹרֵר בְּפֶסַח קְדוּשַּׁת יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ סוֹפְרִין שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע לִהְיוֹת מְזוּקָּק שִׁבְעָתַיִם,
for after the sin [of the Golden Calf], every year the holiness of the Exodus awakens on Pesach, and afterward we count seven times seven to be refined sevenfold,
וְאִם יִזְכּוּ יְכוֹלִים בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת לִזְכּוֹת לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ בְּלוּחוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת.
and if they merit, on Shavuos they can attain the Giving of the Torah just as at the First Tablets.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבַקְּשִׁים: יְתוּקַּן מַה שֶּׁפָּגַמְתִּי בִּסְפִירָה פְּלוֹנִית הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לְאוֹתוֹ לַיְלָה, וְאֶטָּהֵר וְאֶתְקַדֵּשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁל מַעְלָה.
And afterward we petition: "May whatever I have blemished in that specific Sefirah pertaining to this night be rectified, and may I be purified and sanctified with the holiness from on high."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
And this follows what they said
(יְרוּשַׁלְמִי שְׁקָלִים פֶּרֶק ג' הֲלָכָה ג')
(Yerushalmi Shekalim 3:3)
עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: טָהֳרָה מְבִיאָה לִידֵי קְדוּשָּׁה, דִּכְתִיב
regarding the teaching that purity leads to holiness, as it is written
(וַיִּקְרָא ט"ז, י"ט):
(Vayikra 16:19):
וְטִהֲרוֹ וְקִדְּשׁוֹ.
"And he shall purify it and sanctify it."
וְקֹדֶשׁ עִילָּאָה הִיא חָכְמָה
And Supernal Holiness (Kodesh Ila'ah) is Chochmah
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' ס"א.),
(Zohar, Vol. 3, 61a),
וְהִיא מַאֲמַר יְהִי אוֹר, וְחָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים אוֹרָה כְּתִיב בְּפָרָשַׁת יְהִי אוֹר כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה
which is the utterance "Let there be light," where "light" is written five times corresponding to the Five Books of the Torah
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ג', ה'),
(Bereishis Rabbah 3:5),
וְזֶהוּ "וְאֶתְקַדֵּשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁל מַעְלָה", קֹדֶשׁ עִילָּאָה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
and this is "and may I be sanctified with the holiness from on high"—Supernal Holiness, the Written Torah.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אוֹמְרִים: וּלְתַקֵּן נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ וְרוּחוֹתֵינוּ וְנִשְׁמוֹתֵינוּ מִכָּל סִיג וּפְגָם
And afterward we recite: "and to rectify our nefashos, our ruchos, and our neshamos from every dross and blemish"
הִיא דְּיֵשׁ חָמֵשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ: נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה, חַיָּה, יְחִידָה
because there are five levels in the soul: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah
(דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ב', ל"ו):
(Devarim Rabbah 2:36):
נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה כְּנֶגֶד אוֹתִיּוֹת ה' ו' ה' שֶׁבְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה,
Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah correspond to the letters Hei, Vav, and Hei of the Name Havayah,
וּנְשָׁמָה לִנְשָׁמָה כּוֹלֵל חַיָּה וִיחִידָה, וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יוּ"ד וְתָגוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְכֶתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
while "the soul of the soul" includes Chayah and Yechidah, corresponding to the Yud and the upper crown-tip of the Yud, which alludes to Kesser Elyon
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' י': ס"ה:).
(Zohar, Vol. 3, 10b, 65b).
וְשָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשָׁה הָאָבוֹת,
And the three levels Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah correspond to the holiness of the three Patriarchs,
שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשֵׁי הַקְּלִיפּוֹת: הַקִּנְאָה וְהַתַּאֲוָה וְהַכָּבוֹד, שֶׁהֵם קְלִיפּוֹת עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל, וַעֲמָלֵק רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה.
who stand against the three primary husks—envy, lust, and honor—which are the husks of Esav, Yishmael, and Amalek, the firstborn of impurity.
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת גְּדוּלָּה חֶסֶד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
Our father Avraham is a chariot for the attribute of Gedulah/Chessed, as it is said
(מִיכָה ז', כ'):
(Michah 7:20):
חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם,
"Kindness to Avraham,"
וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת חֶסֶד עַד כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, וְחֶסֶד עִילָּאָה נָפְקָא מֵחָכְמָה
and the expansion of Chessed reaches up to Kesser Elyon, while Supernal Chessed emerges from Chochmah
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' קע"ה:),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 175b),
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and so it is written in the holy Zohar
(ibid. 14b):
עֲבִיד לְאַבְרָהָם בְּרָזָא דְּחָכְמָה וְכוּלֵּי,
"He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah, etc.,"
וּכְתִיב
and it is written
(מִשְׁלֵי כ', כ"ז):
(Mishlei 20:27):
נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם;
"The candle of Hashem is the neshamah of man";
יִצְחָק מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת גְּבוּרָה, פַּחַד יִצְחָק, וּגְבוּרָה עִילָּאָה נָפְקָא מִבִּינָה
Yitzchak is a chariot for the attribute of Gevurah, "the Fear of Yitzchak," and Supernal Gevurah emerges from Binah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא שָׁם),
(as brought there),
לְיִצְחָק בְּרָזָא דִּתְבוּנָה
"to Yitzchak in the secret of Understanding (Tevunah)"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא שָׁם),
(as brought there),
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד רוּחַ שֶׁבַּלֵּב, דְּשָׁם שְׁנֵי חַלְלֵי הַלֵּב: לֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ וְלֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ;
and he corresponds to Ruach in the heart, where the two chambers of the heart reside: "a wise man's heart at his right and a fool's heart at his left";
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא,
and our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, is the Central Pillar,
וְהַיְינוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת: ש' רָזָא דִּתְלַת אֲבָהָן וּבַת מִתְעַטְּרָא בְּהוּ
which is the holiness of Shabbos: Shin is the secret of the three Patriarchs and Bas (the Daughter, Malchus/Nefesh) is crowned by them
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ר"ד.),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 204a),
וְכֵן ש' תְּלַת כִּתְרִין: כֶּתֶר חָכְמָה בִּינָה וּבַת רְבִיעָא לוֹן
and likewise Shin represents the three crowns—Kesser, Chochmah, Binah—with Bas as the fourth to them
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא חֵלֶק ג' רנ"ז.).
(Ra'aya Mehemna, Vol. 3, 257a).
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: לְתַקֵּן נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ וְרוּחוֹתֵינוּ וְנִשְׁמוֹתֵינוּ מִכָּל סִיג וּפְגָם
And this is why we say "to rectify our nefashos, our ruchos, and our neshamos from every dross and blemish"
לִזְכּוֹת לִהְיוֹת מִתְעַטְּרָא בְּאֲבָהָן שֶׁהֵם עֲנָפִים מִשָּׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
so as to merit being crowned with the Patriarchs, who are branches of the first three Sefiros
וּלְטַהֲרֵנוּ וּלְקַדְּשֵׁנוּ בִּקְדוּשָׁתְךָ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה:
"and to purify us and sanctify us with Your Supernal Holiness":
"עֶלְיוֹן" מוֹרֶה בְּלִי שִׁיעוּר, וְהַיְינוּ כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁהוּא נֶעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם.
"Supernal" (elyon) indicates without measure, referring to Kesser Elyon which is concealed from all thought, just as it was at the Giving of the Torah: "I said, you are angelic beings."

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִצְוַת סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר הִיא כְּעֵין סְפִירַת שִׁבְעָה נְקִיִּים שֶׁל הָאִשָּׁה, וְהִיא הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Chaim Tirer of Chernovitz, Be'er Mayim Chaim, Shemos 19:1 — “At the redemption Hashem suddenly shone upon them a great light, until they reached a wondrous level, without toil and without washing and purifying themselves of the filth of impurity that clung to them. But such a thing does not endure, since it did not come from their own service; therefore it was taken from them immediately after the first day. They were then commanded to count the Omer, seven complete weeks, to wash and purify their souls and bodies of every aspect of impurity and filth, like the law of a niddah who must count seven clean days.” Connection: Like Rav Tzadok, the Be'er Mayim Chaim reads the counting as the seven clean days of purification before Matan Torah; he adds that the holiness of Pesach night was a gift from above that had to be earned afterward through the counting.

But such a thing does not endure, since it did not come from their own service; therefore it was taken from them immediately after the first day. They were then commanded to count the Omer, seven complete weeks, to wash and purify their souls and bodies of every aspect of impurity and filth, like the law of a niddah who must count seven clean days.” Connection: Like Rav Tzadok, the Be'er Mayim Chaim reads the counting as the seven clean days of purification before Matan Torah; he adds that the holiness of Pesach night was a gift from above that had to be earned afterward through the counting.

Rashi: "this disputes" — the view that the filth did not cease until Sinai.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayetzei 4 — “Avraham and Yitzchak surely also repaired the serpent’s corruption, yet the repair was not completed, for dross still came from their seed; only Yaakov was like Adam before the corruption… And so in Shabbos 146a: until three generations the filth did not cease from our forefathers; and though it says ‘until Sinai,’ that is only for his descendants, for whom it ceased at the Giving of the Torah, as we said that both are the words of the living God; but Yaakov from his own side was like Adam before the corruption… and his bed was complete, the twelve tribes without blemish. Still there remain claims on his seed from the serpent’s defilement until Mashiach comes, who will repair everything.” Connection: The same reconciliation of the two views in Shabbos 146a, adding that the final removal of the serpent’s filth from all Israel awaits Mashiach.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tiferes Yosef, Shavuos — “When a person breaks through the concealment by Torah and service, he returns to the light the creation had before; the only difference is that now it comes through human service and the service is called by the worker’s name. This is called ‘third’: what the light the creation had before has become firmly acquired through its service, as in Shabbos 146a, until three generations the filth did not cease from our forefathers… Torah is so called because it reveals what was hidden; through Torah and service they came back to the light Hashem had concealed, and it became their full acquisition.” Connection: Tiferes Yosef also joins Shabbos 146a to Sinai; it adds that the filth ceases when the earlier light is regained as Israel’s own acquisition through service, in line with the counting as self-refinement.
